texts: good. the collecting event carries Pell as agent, the silken threads as what is taken, the Cliff Path lanterns as the source, and dawn plus day 1 of Year 1 as the time; 'Cliff Path' stays one name and is typed as a path.

good. the landing, the moths as a group, the lanterns and the night slot are all recorded, and the moth group is the same symbol the next sentence reuses. the reviewer's complaint that 'had landed' records no before-ordering against Pell's collecting was refuted on adjudication — this sentence holds only one event, so no ordering is owed — so nothing here needs rewriting.

good. the leaving reuses the same moths and, usefully, the same thread group Pell collects in sentence 1, so the threads left on the lanterns and the threads carried to Cauldron Hall are one set. the missing before-ordering against the collecting was likewise refuted, not a defect.
good. the carrying has Pell, the same thread group, and Cauldron Hall as the destination, kept as one name and typed as a hall.

good. all of it lands: Hesper as agent, the three cauldrons as a counted group, the sea-water as the means with its origin attached as a from-relation to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools, and the pools named and typed as tide-pools. (the pools being plural has no carrier of its own — a multi-word name is one individual — but nothing your sentence states is lost.)
good. the boiling has Hesper, the same thread group as its object and the same sea-water as its location, so the whole chain from lanterns to cauldron hangs together on one set of symbols.

mixed: the rule itself is well-formed and can fire — for every cauldron in the group, a forming event with mire-essence in it by evening. but 'in each cauldron' makes that essence a per-cauldron term that exists only inside the rule, so nothing outside the rule can point back at it, which is what breaks sentence 8. unless you specifically need the per-cauldron reading, write 'Mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.' — same content, and the essence becomes one entity later sentences can refer to.

mixed: the storing, Hesper, the three clay vessels and the location are all right, but 'the mire-essence' finds no antecedent it can reach, because sentence 7's essence lives only inside a per-cauldron rule. the parse therefore mints a fresh, unrelated essence, so the stuff stored is not the stuff that formed. rewriting the previous sentence as 'Mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.' makes this sentence bind correctly with no change to its own wording.
